name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Womack's 15-to-1 fundraising advantage and $2.4M war chest
Challenger Ryerse raised only $120K with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Womack at roughly 95%
model.rationale: Womack is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 13 points, while Ryerse has raised little and lacks outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican win, so the forecast sits near the safe-Republican threshold.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Womack or an unusually strong Democratic national environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Steve Womack seeks another term in a northwest Arkansas district that has voted Republican by double digits. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.9 million and holding $2.4 million on hand, while Democrat Robb Ryerse has raised roughly $120,000 and reports only about $6,000 in the bank. No outside groups are active on either side, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Womack about a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's Republican lean and his incumbency. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot. The race is expected to remain low-cost and low-profile, with Womack heavily favored to return to Congress.
